title: Design strict one-way parent-to-child VM sharing; investigate MCP
objective: Define the initial strict push-only parent-to-child data-sharing contract and investigate read-only MCP resources as a possible future alternative, including benefits, request-metadata directionality, implementation options, and security tradeoffs.

acceptance_criteria.text: Record the current direction as strict push-only parent-to-child sharing: a parent-selected snapshot is delivered to a child, with no child request, response, or control metadata on the sharing channel. Revisit this direction only through an explicit owner decision.
Define a versioned, size-bounded snapshot schema with provenance and sensitivity metadata; the parent selects and validates records, and the child cannot enumerate or access unshared records.

Investigate read-only MCP resources as a future alternative: document what MCP could bring (common resource shape, discovery/interoperability, tooling), its implementation and authorization needs, and the request/URI/control metadata sent upward. State the security tradeoffs and conditions required before reconsidering strict one-way semantics; do not implement MCP as the current sharing path.

Compare push-snapshot delivery options and specify per-child integrity/authenticity, read-only handling, size/expiry/revocation, and how delivery avoids arbitrary parent filesystem, command, Docker, network, credential, or write access.
Specify recursive behavior: each child receives only data explicitly selected by its immediate parent; descendants receive no inherited parent/ancestor channel or authority.

Record the decision and limits in VM architecture docs and define adversarial tests for snapshot tampering/scope, write attempts, path/URI abuse, child depth/reset, and transport isolation before implementation is accepted.

needed: Inventory current host/guest crossings and browser-auth MCP capability; identify whether any existing channel can expose parent state beyond its intended purpose.
Compare read-only MCP resources with a push-only schema-validated snapshot for strict one-way data flow; document the request-metadata direction tradeoff.
Define adversarial integration tests proving a child cannot read unshared parent data, mutate parent state, invoke arbitrary host actions, or access ancestor channels.
Design a strict push-only snapshot path and verify the child cannot send requests or control metadata over the sharing channel.

Compare read-only MCP resources with push-only snapshots for common schema/discovery benefits, implementation complexity, authorization, and request-metadata leakage; treat MCP only as a future option.
Define adversarial integration tests proving a child cannot read unshared parent data, mutate parent state, invoke arbitrary parent actions, or access ancestor channels.
